question: How does BSP scale CET across the Northeast?
html:
BSP scales CET in three phases. First, make Massachusetts and Connecticut one company around Horton's wastewater work. Next, buy founder-owned contractors in RI, NH, ME and VT. Then shift the mix toward recurring service contracts, which is where the multiple moves (CET growth plan). The model follows Smith + Howard, which grew about 4x in roughly 3.7 years. The target for CET is about 3x in 36 months.

Phase 1: Make Horton count

  • Combine MA and CT into one operating company.
  • Point Horton at 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects across CT, MA and RI. New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk lead the list (CET growth plan).
  • The radar's priority prime targets are funded CT pump-station programs (CET opportunity radar):
  • Fairfield (~$36M est. value)
  • West Haven ($30M)
  • South Windsor ($18M)
  • Danbury electrical resiliency (~$3.2M)
  • Several October bids on the radar have already closed. These include the Massport Worcester RFQ (Oct 8, 2026) and Glastonbury (Oct 6, 2026). Still open:
  • Union Station generator (Oct 28, 2026)
  • MassDOT NEVI installer call (to Oct 31, 2026)
  • Cambridge EV charging (Nov 10, 2026)
  • MassWildlife hatchery generators (Nov 25, 2026)

Phase 2: Buy into the north

  • CET's existing six-state licensing lets it enter RI, NH, ME and VT through add-ons (CET growth plan).
  • The aim is to get there before Pfingsten's NEC Group, Ridgemont's Crete United or other sponsor companies.
  • The add-on screen holds 48 companies. Its revenue median is about $15.1M, based on ZoomInfo modelled estimates that need diligence (CET add-on targets).
  • The ranked top 10 is mostly in Massachusetts. Only CTEC Solar is in Connecticut. McDonald Electrical (rank 1) brings RI and CT reach through its ANJ Electric division.
  • A northern-state target list would need a separate ranking.
  • Radar coverage is also thin in the north: RI has 4 items and NH has 5, against 27 for CT (CET opportunity radar).

Phase 3: Build recurring service revenue

  • Target service lines: SCADA and pump-station monitoring, solar and storage O&M, EV depot charging, and NuWave efficiency work.
  • PKF and Capstone price this mix 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors (CET growth plan).
  • Data-center electrical is real upside in PJM. In New England it is thin; ISO-NE says growth there has lagged other regions.

Roadmap targets (all est.)

MonthRevenueEBITDAHeadcountLocations
0$80M$8.0M2754
12$115M$12.1M3907
24$170M$19.5M56010
36$240M$30.0M78013
  • Every baseline is a low-confidence analyst estimate from public filings. None is disclosed by CET or BSP (CET growth plan).
  • Month 36 assumes a 12.5% margin and about 25% recurring service mix.
  • Validating these figures needs audited CET financials and Horton's backlog.

Next actions

  1. Submit the Union Station generator bid and the MassDOT NEVI installer response before Oct 31, 2026.
  2. Book engineer-of-record meetings for the Fairfield, West Haven, South Windsor and Danbury programs.
  3. Re-rank the 48-company add-on screen for RI, NH, ME and VT, and verify ZoomInfo revenue against headcount.
  4. Pull the MassDEP 2026 clean-water project tables by hand. The radar could not itemize the 76 projects worth about $1.02B (CET opportunity radar).
